reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, aggregate rubric, fresh-review framework, Goal resource-review context, Goal StructureDefinition report, relevant R4/R6 Goal element definitions, and behavior reports for findings whose `affectedResources` include `Goal`. The deterministic aggregate was used only as a comparison after forming the resource-level judgment.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 Goal is trial-use/FMM 2, so it does not carry normative or high-FMM compatibility pressure. That neutral baseline does not make the breaks unimportant: Goal status, attribution, and outcome information are clinically meaningful care-planning content, so the concrete migration mechanism and avoidability still drive the review.

overall.oneLineConclusion: Goal keeps its resource identity, but R4 instances using status, attribution, or outcome fields need a targeted R6 migration program; that does not eliminate the value of preserving avoidable compatibility where low-cost.

reasoning.thesisMd: Goal is not removed or replaced, and much of the core resource shape remains recognizable. The resource-level break is nevertheless real because four R4 paths become old-valid/new-invalid in R6: `statusReason`, `statusDate`, `expressedBy`, and `outcomeCode`/`outcomeReference`. The strongest concerns are not the count alone but the kind of migration: `statusDate` narrows from lifecycle-status timing to achievement-status timing, `expressedBy` is renamed even though the source concept remains, and Goal outcome content disappears without a direct R6 Goal replacement.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The actual migration shape is a moderate targeted remodel, not a full resource redesign. Implementations can keep using the Goal resource in R6, but they cannot rely on same-name copying for several clinically relevant optional elements. Some transformations are mechanical or near-mechanical, such as mapping a text `statusReason` into one `lifecycleStatusReason.text`; others require policy or review, especially lifecycle cancellation/creation dates and outcome data with no direct R6 field.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A resource-level migration program is partially unavoidable for any implementation that used the affected R4 fields. That only modestly lowers the leverage of preventing additional breaks: preserving or formally mapping low-cost legacy paths would still reduce data-loss risk and implementation cost. The right posture is not `migration-program-dominates`; it is to expect Goal migration while still revisiting changes that look avoidable or lack a computable replacement.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The most valuable low-cost preservation candidates are keeping `statusDate` for lifecycle-status timing while adding `achievementStatusDate`, keeping or aliasing `expressedBy` as the source/establishing-party element while adding `recorder`, and retaining deprecated outcome elements for a transition or defining a formal replacement relationship before removal. `statusReason` is less compelling as a revisit item because retaining both the old string and the new repeatable `CodeableConcept` creates duplicate same-fact representations. The R6-only additions (`acceptance`, `continuous`, widened `addresses`, and `lifecycleStatus=unknown`) are mostly reverse-conversion concerns, not reasons to block the R6 design.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding was found with `Goal` in `affectedResources`. The 11 shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings are real ecosystem context, but under the review rules they remain context only for Goal and do not drive the Goal resource-level conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The independent conclusion agrees with the deterministic aggregate on `Partial` migration unavoidability, `moderate-targeted-remodel`, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`. The important nuance is that the aggregate count should not be used to discount the three Revisit findings: the targeted migration burden is exactly why official mappings or low-cost preservation would matter.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the structural deltas because the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions directly show the changed paths. The main uncertainty is intent and prevalence: no official cross-version Goal mapping or design rationale was available, and this review did not measure how often production R4 Goals populate the optional affected fields.

findingConsiderations.title: Goal.statusDate was replaced by achievementStatusDate with narrower semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a hard old-valid/new-invalid path removal and a semantic narrowing. R4 `statusDate` covered lifecycle-status timing such as creation, achievement, and cancellation, while R6 `achievementStatusDate` is achievement-status timing. Blind renaming can misstate cancellation or creation dates, so this is a non-mechanical migration and a standards-review-worthy preservation candidate.

findingConsiderations.title: Goal.expressedBy was replaced by source and a new recorder element
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `expressedBy` and R6 `source` appear to carry the same establishing-party/source concept, while `recorder` is an added responsibility concept. R6 could likely have widened and clarified the old element while adding `recorder`; the current rename creates a wire-name and generated-code break with limited apparent benefit.

findingConsiderations.title: Goal outcomeCode and outcomeReference were removed without a direct R6 Goal replacement
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the highest data-loss concern. R4 Goal outcome code/reference content is clinically meaningful and R6 provides no direct Goal element replacement, so migration may require extensions, Observation relationship policy, notes, or profile-specific rules. A transitional deprecation or formal replacement mapping would materially reduce risk.

findingConsiderations.title: Goal.statusReason was replaced by repeating CodeableConcept lifecycleStatusReason
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This contributes to the need for Goal transforms because R4 instances using `statusReason` are invalid in R6. However, ordinary forward migration is direct by placing the string in `lifecycleStatusReason.text`, and the R6 repeatable coded representation has a clear model benefit. Keeping both fields would create same-fact duplication, so this is mostly a local migration chore rather than a key revisit driver.

findingConsiderations.title: Goal.lifecycleStatus required value set adds the R6-only code unknown
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The required binding is widened for R4-to-R6: all R4 lifecycle-status codes remain valid. The new `unknown` code creates down-conversion policy for R6 data but does not make R4 Goal instances invalid, so it does not drive the migration-program conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds a structured Goal.acceptance backbone with required participant when present
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `acceptance` is optional and additive. Its required `participant` applies only if an R6 acceptance entry is created, so it is a reverse-conversion/codegen consideration rather than an R4-to-R6 break.

findingConsiderations.title: Goal.addresses adds MedicationRequest, Procedure, and NutritionIntake reference targets
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The reference target list is widened and preserves R4 targets. It may matter for R6-to-R4 conversion when new targets are used, but it is not a forward compatibility break and does not need a less-breaking R6 design.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds Goal.continuous sustainment semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `continuous` is an optional new semantic flag. Existing R4 Goal instances remain acceptable with respect to this addition, and any loss is limited to plain R6-to-R4 down-conversion of new content.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource-level operation finding can affect APIs used around Goal instances, but it is not a Goal-specific behavior finding and `Goal` was not listed directly in behavior `affectedResources`. It was therefore considered as ecosystem context only and not scored into the Goal resource conclusion.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit removal of `Goal.outcomeCode` and `Goal.outcomeReference`: either retain them as deprecated transition elements for R6 or publish a computable replacement relationship that preserves existing outcome data without local guesswork.

Revisit `Goal.statusDate` narrowing: keep a lifecycle-status date path or provide explicit rules distinguishing dates that may map to `achievementStatusDate` from cancellation, rejection, creation, or other lifecycle dates that need another representation.

Revisit the `expressedBy` to `source` rename. If the semantic role is the same, consider retaining the R4 name with widened targets and clearer prose while adding `recorder` separately, or at least define a formal alias/mapping.

Publish official R4-to-R6 Goal migration guidance or StructureMap covering `statusReason`, `statusDate`, `expressedBy`/`source`/`recorder`, and outcome handling, because several changes are not safe same-name copies.

caveats: No official Goal-specific R4-to-R6 ConceptMap, StructureMap, or design rationale was available in the supplied inputs.
The review did not measure production prevalence of optional R4 Goal fields, so impact estimates are based on structural mechanism and clinical significance rather than usage telemetry.
The R6 evidence is from the 6.0.0-ballot4 package; later ballot or publication changes could alter the conclusions.
